# What Perplexity API keys the library redacts, and what it leaves alone.
#
# Every key here is built from the ordered run
# 0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz, which no real credential is. That run is
# thirty-six characters, so a body carries it and twelve characters more — the
# shortest body the pattern reads, since the count is a floor. It is spelled in
# lowercase where the case does not matter and in uppercase where the case is
# what a case is about: base62 holds the letters of both, so either spelling is
# a body. The one case the run cannot state is "a body of one repeated
# character", which is written from a single letter because what it turns on is
# the entropy of a body and the run has plenty.

patterns: perplexity-api-key

# The one prefix Perplexity has issued an API key with. There is a single kind
# of string here rather than a table of them: one key authenticates every
# request an account makes against one balance, so nothing in the value says
# what it may be spent on, and the cases below are that one shape in the places
# a key is written.

case:     a key in an environment assignment
in:       PERPLEXITY_API_KEY=pplx-0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789ab
out:      PERPLEXITY_API_KEY=«perplexity-api-key»

case:     a key in the bearer authorization header the api is called with
in:       Authorization: Bearer pplx-0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789ab
out:      Authorization: Bearer «perplexity-api-key»

case:     a key in the json the endpoint that issues one returns
in:       {"auth_token":"pplx-0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789ab","token_name":"Production API Key"}
out:      {"auth_token":"«perplexity-api-key»","token_name":"Production API Key"}

case:     a key on a command line
in:       curl -H "Authorization: Bearer pplx-0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789ab" https://api.perplexity.ai/chat/completions
out:      curl -H "Authorization: Bearer «perplexity-api-key»" https://api.perplexity.ai/chat/completions

case:     a key in a configuration environment block
in:       "env": {"PERPLEXITY_API_KEY": "pplx-0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789ab"}
out:      "env": {"PERPLEXITY_API_KEY": "«perplexity-api-key»"}

# The alphabet the forty-eight characters are written in. It is base62 — the
# letters of both cases and the digits — which is what the published expression
# admits behind the prefix. The two characters base64url adds, the hyphen and
# the underscore, are not admitted, and either of them ends a body.

case:     a body written in capitals
in:       pplx-0123456789ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456789AB
out:      «perplexity-api-key»

case:     a body carrying a hyphen
in:       pplx-0123456789abcdefghij-lmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789ab
out:      pplx-0123456789abcdefghij-lmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789ab

case:     a body carrying an underscore
in:       pplx-0123456789abcdefghij_lmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789ab
out:      pplx-0123456789abcdefghij_lmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789ab

# The lengths either side of forty-eight. Perplexity states no length for a key,
# and no alphabet and no checksum either; one expression is published for the
# format and it reads forty-eight characters. The count is read as a floor
# rather than exactly: forty-seven characters are not a key, and forty-nine are
# one key to the end of its run rather than a key and a character left over.
# What the floor costs is the middle case below — a key cut short of forty-eight
# keeps every random character written in front of the cut, and none of them is
# redacted.

case:     a body of forty-eight characters is a key
in:       pplx-0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789ab
out:      «perplexity-api-key»

case:     a body of forty-seven characters is not
in:       pplx-0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789a
out:      pplx-0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789a

case:     an alphabet run longer than the floor is a key to the end of it
in:       pplx-0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789abc
out:      «perplexity-api-key»

# The entropy floor the published rules carry is not read. This library redacts
# rather than reports, so a value declined is a credential written out in full
# where a value taken wrongly is a stretch of opaque text lost to a reader — and
# nothing about the format says a key of repetitive characters cannot be issued.
# The case below is what reading no entropy admits, and it is the one here whose
# body is not the ordered run: the run carries more entropy than either rule
# asks for, so no other case in this file would report a scan that started
# reading one.

case:     a body of one repeated character
in:       pplx-aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa
out:      «perplexity-api-key»

# What a key may be written against. There is no boundary on either side of the
# prefix, so a key keeps its span whatever word character it abuts — and where
# the run of its alphabet carries on past the floor, what carries it on is
# redacted with the key. A hyphen and an underscore end the run instead.

case:     a key after an underscore
in:       PERPLEXITY_API_KEY_pplx-0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789ab
out:      PERPLEXITY_API_KEY_«perplexity-api-key»

case:     a key after a letter
in:       xpplx-0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789ab
out:      x«perplexity-api-key»

case:     a word written against a key
in:       pplx-0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789absuffix
out:      «perplexity-api-key»

case:     a hyphenated word written against a key
in:       pplx-0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789ab-suffix
out:      «perplexity-api-key»-suffix

case:     an underscored word written against a key
in:       pplx-0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789ab_suffix
out:      «perplexity-api-key»_suffix

case:     a key at the end of a sentence
in:       the key is pplx-0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789ab.
out:      the key is «perplexity-api-key».

# Two keys written together. The four letters the prefix opens with belong to
# the alphabet a body is written in, so a body may close with pplx and the
# hyphen of the next key stand directly behind it; the second key begins four
# characters before the first one ends, the two spans overlap and are redacted
# as one. Written with nothing at all between them the first body reaches four
# characters into the second prefix and stops at the hyphen behind them, so
# those two overlap as well. Written with a space between them the two are
# separate values, and both go.

case:     a key beginning inside the key before it
in:       pplx-0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz01234567pplx-0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789ab
out:      «perplexity-api-key»

case:     two keys with nothing between them
in:       pplx-0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789abpplx-0123456789ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456789AB
out:      «perplexity-api-key»

case:     two keys separated by a space
in:       pplx-0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789ab pplx-0123456789ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456789AB
out:      «perplexity-api-key» «perplexity-api-key»

# Perplexity names its own products with the prefix it issues keys under, so the
# text most likely to be written beside a key carries a whole prefix. The API was
# announced as pplx-api, the embedding models are pplx-embed-v1-0 and
# pplx-embed-context-v1-0, the command line is pplx-cli and ships as
# pplx-aarch64-apple-darwin.bin, and the MCP server names itself pplx-mcp-server
# in a header of its own. What holds each of them away is the floor: the segment
# behind the prefix is broken by the next hyphen or dot long before forty-eight
# characters. The last case is what that leaves admitted, and it is a key's
# format exactly.

case:     the name the api was announced under
in:       using pplx-api for search
out:      using pplx-api for search

case:     the embedding model names
in:       {"model":"pplx-embed-v1-0"} {"model":"pplx-embed-context-v1-0"}
out:      {"model":"pplx-embed-v1-0"} {"model":"pplx-embed-context-v1-0"}

case:     the command line and the file it ships as
in:       pplx-cli installs pplx-aarch64-apple-darwin.bin
out:      pplx-cli installs pplx-aarch64-apple-darwin.bin

case:     the name the mcp server sends as its source
in:       "X-Source": "pplx-mcp-server"
out:      "X-Source": "pplx-mcp-server"

case:     a name whose segment runs the length of a body
in:       {"model":"pplx-0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789ab"}
out:      {"model":"«perplexity-api-key»"}

# What this pattern redacts that nobody issued. The prefix closes with a hyphen,
# which standard base64 writes nowhere, so only a base64url encoding can hold
# one — and where forty-eight base62 characters follow, the run from the prefix
# to the end of them is redacted whether or not Perplexity issued it. That is
# the answer rather than a fault in it, because such a run is a key's format
# exactly and nothing in the text tells the two apart: sparing these would spare
# a real key written the same way. What is taken is a stretch of a value that
# was already opaque to a reader.

case:     the prefix inside a longer run of base64url
in:       payload=zzzzpplx-0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789abzzzz
out:      payload=zzzz«perplexity-api-key»

case:     the prefix where a signature stands
in:       eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9.eyJzdWIiOiJhYmMifQ.zzzzpplx-0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789abzzzz
out:      eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9.eyJzdWIiOiJhYmMifQ.zzzz«perplexity-api-key»

# A digest written behind the prefix, which is the one over-match here that
# takes a value a reader had a use for. Hexadecimal digits are base62 and a
# digest carries nothing that ends a run, so pplx- and the sixty-four characters
# of a SHA-256 are a key's format exactly, and both are redacted. Declining them
# would mean declining every key Perplexity happened to write in the digits
# alone, which is a whole credential against a cache key. What holds either side
# of it is the floor and the prefix: a SHA-1 is forty characters, eight short of
# a body, an MD5 is thirty-two, and an underscore is no character the prefix
# carries.

case:     a sha256 behind the prefix
in:       pplx-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      «perplexity-api-key»

case:     a sha256 in a cache key
in:       key: pplx-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      key: «perplexity-api-key»

case:     a sha1 behind the prefix, eight characters short of a body
in:       pplx-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      pplx-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567

case:     an md5 behind the prefix
in:       pplx-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      pplx-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef

case:     a sha256 behind an underscore rather than the prefix
in:       pplx_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      pplx_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef

# And what this pattern leaves alone. The first three are the prefix, read in
# the case Perplexity writes it — including the capitalisation its own MCP
# server writes in a header name — in the hyphen it closes with and in that
# hyphen being there at all. The two after them are the alphabet and the anchor:
# a body a space has broken, and a run of the right length with no prefix in
# front of it. The last two hold no hyphen where the prefix wants one, so
# neither holds a position to be found at however long it runs.

case:     an uppercase prefix
in:       PPLX-0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789ab
out:      PPLX-0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789ab

case:     the prefix capitalised as a header name writes it
in:       Pplx-0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789ab
out:      Pplx-0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789ab

case:     an underscore where the prefix carries a hyphen
in:       pplx_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789ab
out:      pplx_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789ab

case:     the prefix without its closing hyphen
in:       pplx0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789ab
out:      pplx0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789ab

case:     a body broken by a space
in:       pplx-0123456789abcdefghij lmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789ab
out:      pplx-0123456789abcdefghij lmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789ab

case:     a run of the right length opening with no prefix
in:       0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789ab
out:      0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789ab

case:     a hexadecimal digest
in:       sha1=0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      sha1=0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567

case:     prose
in:       there is no credential in this sentence
out:      there is no credential in this sentence
